items.title: What Are Applied Materials Stock Investors Overlooking?
items.summary: Applied Materials (AMAT) sold a record $7 billion of chipmaking tools in fiscal Q3 2026. That was about 77% of its $9.1 billion in revenue for the quarter. When you own the stock, you mostly own those tool sales. A record that large is easy to read as the new normal. So what might Applied Materials investors be overlooking about those tool sales.

items.title: How Investors May Respond To Microchip Technology (MCHP) Expanding 10BASE-T1S Ethernet For Zonal Edge Architectures

items.title: Microchip Technology (MCHP) Stock Trades Up, Here Is Why
items.summary: Shares of analog chipmaker Microchip Technology (NASDAQ:MCHP) jumped 1.9% in the afternoon session after the company announced the expansion of its 10BASE-T1S Single Pair Ethernet portfolio with new transceivers and endpoint devices.

items.title: Is Applied Materials Still The Business You Bought?
items.summary: You may own Applied Materials (AMAT) as a chip equipment maker that aims to hand most of its spare cash back to shareholders. A $10,000 holding a year ago is now worth about $24,500. Your stake in this business is far bigger than it was. Is Applied Materials still the business you bought.

items.title: ON Semiconductor Stock Looks Expensive Until You Price Its Fuller Factories
items.summary: ON Semiconductor (ON) makes power and sensing chips for cars, industrial equipment and AI data centers. The stock trades at about 27.6 times trailing adjusted earnings, meaning normalized net income with stock-based compensation added back. That basis is meant to sit closer to the one analysts use in their forecasts than GAAP earnings would, though the two are not defined identically. At that multiple the stock looks expensive. But the trailing year was weak, and the weakness is fading.
